title: South Korean leisure and group participation rebound while generalized social trust declines
source_unit: Statistics Korea, 2025 Social Survey: welfare, social participation, leisure, income and consumption, and labor
geography: South Korea; residents aged 13 or 19 and over depending on the module, with two-year comparisons to 2023

observations.period: 2025; leisure and cultural participation in the previous 12 months, compared with 2023

denominator.unit: Statistics Korea Social Survey respondents; module denominators vary by age and question and are not disclosed in the public summary used here

domestic_travel.unit: percent with domestic tourism travel experience

cultural_art_sport_venue_attendance.unit: percent attending cultural, artistic, or sports events in person

leisure_facility_use.unit: percent using leisure facilities such as tourist attractions, recreation forests, and beaches

book_reading.unit: percent of people aged 13 or over reading at least one book in the previous year

mechanism.value: Post-pandemic leisure recovery is broad but uneven: travel and facility use rose more sharply than cultural venue attendance, while the share reading remained nearly flat and reading intensity declined

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Statistics Korea Social Survey tables 23-1, 23-2, 24, 25, and 26; changes are calculated from the published 2023 and 2025 percentages.
observations.uncertainty: The survey uses annual-recall questions and broad activity categories; it does not establish frequency, spending, affordability, venue supply, travel purpose, quality of experience, or causal post-pandemic recovery.
observations.subgroup: South Korean residents, with age thresholds varying by table; cultural venue attendance and travel measures are annual-recall population shares.
observations.counterinterpretation: Travel and facility increases may reflect pent-up demand, mobility normalization, or category-specific supply; cultural attendance may be constrained by cost, time, health, or substitution into home and digital activity.

observations.period: 2025; social participation, volunteering, trust, and loneliness, compared with 2023 where available

denominator.unit: Statistics Korea Social Survey respondents; social-participation and trust module denominators vary and are not disclosed in the public summary used here

organization_participation.unit: percent participating in at least one organization

general_social_trust.unit: percent saying Korean society can be trusted

loneliness.unit: percent frequently or sometimes feeling lonely

participation_trust_tension.value: Group participation, donation, and volunteering rose while generalized social trust fell

mechanism.value: More organized activity does not automatically translate into generalized trust: people may participate through specific, instrumental, or identity-based groups while broader social confidence declines

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Statistics Korea Social Survey tables 17, 18, 19-1, and 20-1; changes are calculated from the published 2023 and 2025 percentages.
observations.uncertainty: Trust and participation are self-reported cross-sectional measures; the survey does not identify group composition, intensity, reciprocity, institutional performance, political context, or causal direction between participation and trust.
observations.subgroup: South Korean residents aged 19 or over for most social-participation and trust items; exact module eligibility follows the Statistics Korea table definitions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Participation may be concentrated in family, hobby, religious, or professional groups that do not generate generalized trust; trust changes may reflect survey wording, political events, cohort replacement, or response composition.

related_sources.claim: Official Statistics Korea 2025 Social Survey statistical-table workbook used to reproduce tables 17-20 and 23-28.
Official Statistics Korea PDF press release for the 2025 Social Survey headline findings.
Official English-language press release summarizing 2025 leisure, travel, cultural attendance, reading, and preferred leisure activities.

boundary: This record adds a South Korean leisure, cultural-participation, social-organization, trust, and loneliness layer. It does not establish causal recovery, spending, affordability, institutional legitimacy, group quality, cultural belonging, or a contradiction between participation and trust at the individual level.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Statistics Korea release page, statistical-table workbook, PDF release, and English summary reviewed; 2023/2025 values, table definitions, annual-recall windows, age thresholds, and change calculations checked.
